title: The fork: conditions, groups and surprises

steps.title: Part two: a fork in the road
steps.text:
This tutorial carries on from the first one. Your cave gets two ways forward, a [b]door[/b] and a [b]side passage[/b], and both lead into the same hidden area, the [b]Lair[/b], where guards wait. Along the way you meet [b]conditions[/b], the mission's [b]built-in variables[/b], the details of an [b]action[/b], [b]monster groups[/b] and [b]unaware monsters[/b].

Continue with the mission you made in part one, or press [b]Load the example[/b] to start from the one that ships with the game (that replaces the open mission, and asks first if it has unsaved changes).

[color=#9fb4c8]This step is done when the mission has a stage with some floor and a start position.[/color]

steps.title: What we are going to build
steps.text:
From the cave two paths lead east and north-east:

[b]North:[/b] a wide corridor with a [b]door[/b]. Opening it reveals the Lair and spawns the guards, who are [i]aware[/i] and ready to fight.
[b]East:[/b] a [b]side passage[/b] with an exploration token that fires by itself. It also reveals the Lair and spawns the same guards, but they are [i]unaware[/i]: they sleep until something wakes them.

The Lair is a stage of its own that starts hidden, and the group of guards is defined once and used by both routes. A flag, [i]encounter_started[/i], makes sure the guards only appear once, whichever route is taken first.

steps.title: A hidden stage for the Lair
steps.text:
Right-click the mission name in the Outline, choose [b]New Group[/b] and name it [i]Lair[/i]. Then select it and [b]untick Visible[/b] in the panel below the tree: a stage that is not visible stays secret until an effect reveals it. Finally choose it as the [b]Working group[/b] in the toolbar.

[color=#9fb4c8]The stage you start in is shown automatically. Every other stage waits for a Show Stage effect.[/color]

steps.title: The Lair's floor
steps.text:
With the Lair as the working group, place a big floor tile to the east of the cave, about twelve squares from its left edge and a little higher up, for example [b]17a[/b]. It lands in the hidden stage.

[color=#9fb4c8]Do it for me assumes the example cave; if yours differs, place it wherever you like and connect the paths yourself.[/color]

steps.title: Two ways to get there
steps.text:
Switch the working group back to the stage you start in (the cave), then lay the two paths so that everything is [b]one connected floor[/b]:

[b]North:[/b] a corridor going up and east from the top of the cave, two squares wide.
[b]East:[/b] a second one leaving the cave on its east side and curving up into the Lair from below.

Keep a gap of empty squares between the two paths, so they only meet in the Lair. Use whatever tiles you like (this tutorial's tiles: 3a, 15a, 6a and 21a).

steps.title: A door in the north corridor
steps.text:
Open the [b]Prop[/b] tab and place a [b]gate[/b] across the two-wide north corridor (press [b]R[/b] to turn it so it spans the corridor). Then select it in the Outline and give it a name, [i]lair_door[/i]. Names are how you find a prop again in dialogs.

Nothing happens with it yet. A door only does something when it has an [b]action[/b].

steps.title: Remember that the guards came
steps.text:
Both routes can wake up the encounter, but the guards should only ever appear [b]once[/b]. The mission has to remember it happened: a yes/no variable.

Click the mission name in the Outline, press [b]Variables…[/b] and add [i]encounter_started[/i] (type [b]Bool[/b], no at the start).

While the dialog is open, look at the variable list in any condition later on: next to your own variables there are [b]built-in[/b] ones the game keeps up to date by itself: [i]round_number[/i], [i]player_count[/i] and [i]difficulty[/i]. You will use two of them soon.

steps.title: Where the guards stand
steps.text:
Make sure the Lair is the working group again, open [b]Misc[/b], click [b]Monster Spawn[/b] (it starts a new area) and click a few squares at the back of the Lair floor, away from the entrances. The spawn area belongs to the Lair stage, so it stays secret too.

Three squares is a good size: two guards, and one square for the extra guard that joins bigger parties.

steps.title: The door's action
steps.text:
Select the door, press [b]Actions…[/b] and [b]Add Action[/b]. Here is what each field does:

[b]Name[/b]: what the players see and pick (and what voice control listens for). Try [i]Open the door[/i].
[b]Description[/b]: the line shown under the name. Say what happens.
[b]Action id[/b]: a technical name for triggers to listen to. Players never see it.
[b]Single shot[/b]: the action can only be used once. Tick it for a door.
[b]Conditions[/b]: the action is only offered while they hold.
[b]Apply automatically[/b]: no choice, the effects just happen. Leave it off here: we use it for the token.

steps.title: A door that removes itself
steps.text:
An action runs its [b]effects[/b] in order. Add two:

[b]Remove Object[/b] and pick [b]Self[/b] at the top of the object list: the prop the action belongs to. In the real game an open door comes off the board. [i]Self[/i] always means "this prop", so you can copy the action to another prop and it still works.
[b]Show Stage[/b]: pick the Lair. The table is told which pieces to put on the board.

steps.title: The guards, and a bigger party
steps.text:
Add a third effect to the door's action: [b]Spawn Monsters[/b], with your Lair spawn area. Press [b]Monsters…[/b], then [b]Add Monster[/b] twice.

Now the built-in variables: open the second monster's [b]Properties…[/b] and press [b]Spawns always…[/b]. Add the condition [b]player_count >= 3[/b]. That guard only appears when three or more heroes play.

[color=#9fb4c8]The same trick scales difficulty: Mission > Monster levels… lets a formula such as difficulty - 2 raise or lower every monster's level.[/color]

steps.title: Only spawn once
steps.text:
If the side passage was used first, the guards are already there, so the door must not spawn them a second time. Every effect has its own [b]Conditions…[/b] button: the effect only runs while its conditions hold.

On the Spawn Monsters effect add the condition [b]encounter_started = false[/b]. Then, at the end of the action, add [b]Set Variable[/b]: encounter_started = true.
steps.assist_label: Add the condition and the flag

steps.title: Define the guards once
steps.text:
The side passage must spawn the same guards. You could build the list again, but then every later change has to be made twice. Make it a [b]group[/b] instead.

Open the spawn effect's [b]Monsters…[/b] and press [b]Make a reusable group of this list[/b]. Name it [i]Lair guards[/i]. The button on the effect now reads "Group: Lair guards…". Any Spawn Monsters effect can use a group: edit it in one place and every use follows.
highlight: button:Make a reusable group of this list

steps.title: A token on the east path
steps.text:
Back in the Palette, with the cave stage as working group, place an [b]exploration token[/b] on the east path and name it [i]side_passage[/i].

A token is just a prop that is made for [b]Apply automatically[/b]: dragging a hero onto it fires its action at once, without a choice. The app does not see anyone walking, so the table tells it as usual by dragging a hero onto the token.

steps.title: Sneak in
steps.text:
Select the token, press [b]Actions…[/b] and [b]Add Action[/b]: name [i]Sneak in[/i], with a description. Tick [b]Single shot[/b] and [b]Apply automatically[/b].

Now a condition on the [i]action[/i] this time: [b]encounter_started = false[/b]. Once the guards are out, sneaking in is pointless, so the action is simply not offered any more.

steps.title: Guards who do not know you are there
steps.text:
Give the token's action three effects: [b]Show Stage[/b] (the Lair), [b]Spawn Monsters[/b] and [b]Set Variable[/b] encounter_started = true.

For the spawn pick the Lair spawn area, press [b]Monsters…[/b] and choose [b]Group: Lair guards[/b] as the source. Then press [b]Unaware: no…[/b] and switch it on. The players can see unaware monsters, and attack them, but in the monster phase they do nothing. The whole group wakes up together, [b]when one of them is attacked[/b] or gets a status. That is what the two ticks in that window are for.

steps.title: A noisy door
steps.text:
If the heroes sneak in first and later open the door anyway, the guards should wake. Add one more effect to the door's action: [b]Wake Monsters[/b], leaving the target on all.

It costs nothing when the door was opened first: the guards that spawned are aware already, so there is nobody to wake.

steps.title: Guards get restless
steps.text:
Sleeping guards should not sleep for ever. Click the mission name, press [b]Triggers…[/b] and [b]Add Trigger[/b]: when [b]Before the player phase[/b], with the condition [b]round_number >= 5[/b] and the effect [b]Wake Monsters[/b]. [i]round_number[/i] is one of the built-in variables.

The trigger is checked at the start of every round, and fires once as soon as its condition holds.

steps.title: Ask the checker
steps.text:
Click the [b]Problems[/b] button in the toolbar. Errors are things that cannot work (floating tiles, pieces on empty ground); warnings are worth a look. A mission with errors can still be saved, but the table could not build it.

If something your own tiles caused shows up, press [b]Show[/b] to jump to it.

steps.title: Play both routes
steps.text:
Press [b]Play > Play[/b] (Ctrl+Enter). Before you move anyone, press [b]F9[/b] to take a snapshot.

Take the door first: drag a hero onto it, choose [i]Open the door[/i]. The Lair appears and the guards are ready. Then press [b]F10[/b] to go back and take the side passage instead: the guards sleep. Attack one of them and the whole group wakes. Try Play > Play with 2 heroes and with 4 to see the extra guard come and go.

[b]Ctrl+E[/b] brings you back to the editor.

steps.title: The fork is built
steps.text:
Two routes, one encounter: a hidden stage, a group defined once, an effect that only runs when its conditions hold, built-in variables that change the monsters, and guards that can be asleep.

[b]Peek[/b] shows the finished mission if something behaves differently from yours. The same tools carry bigger missions: more stages that reveal each other, doors that need keys, monsters that wake on a timer.
